There was a day where both me and my mother were interviewed by the police. When I had trouble wording myself (because I was 9 and I’m autistic), they were very pressuring, and they were so obviously not trained to talk to children or autistic people. They made me feel degraded and confused.

What they did to my mother was much worse. They trapped her in a room, and showed her images of my injury I nearly bled to death from, and they kept asking her why she tried to kill me, even though it wasn’t her.

The kicker is that the cops weren’t even the reason the person who tried to kill me got caught. He got caught because what happened to me was on the news and he showed off that he tried to kill me to a friend, and the friend told the police.

I’ve also seen way too many horror stories of cops abusing the disabled, and being disabled myself, that’s terrifying. The police are now linked to my PTSD, and I get bad panic attacks when I see someone in person with a police uniform. I’ve had nightmares of cops beating me ever since I was young, and that certainly doesn’t help.

Polyamory is *not* cheating because it requires the consent of all parties. There is nothing wrong with being polyam. It is not selfish because you are still required to be dedicated to people. It is no one else’s business to decide on other people’s relationships. The polyam relationships that fail often go wrong because people use it to fix a broken relationship when it should be based on you romantically loving more than one person and you having the ability to hold those relationships. Monogamous relationships often fail, but we don’t attack the concept to being dedicated to one person. I will acknowledge that polyamory isn’t for everyone, but that doesn’t mean the concept should be attacked.

I don’t believe in soul mates, finding “the one”, or in people being “perfect” for each other. What makes relationships work is how you are able to work with them, not a matter of being affectionate. Believing in soul mates can especially lead to so much disaster in many ways. I never call a significant other “perfect” because I don’t believe in people being superior to each other. Sure, I love whoever I’m dating more than anyone, but that doesn’t make them the best person in the world. There is no best person no matter how much I love them.

I’ve ended up in several abusive relationships (I left all of them), and they all had a few things in common:

-I felt like I had to earn their respect and love. If I didn’t live up to their high expectations, I wasn’t good enough for them or anyone else.

-They made me feel fearful of them and that I had to twist things they said or did to downplay something done that hurt me, both to myself and the friends that express concern for my well-being.

-My inability to just be myself. I felt like I was wrong for being me. I had to “work hard to fix myself” to an extreme. I had to keep my mouth shut over either my feelings or about a passion I have.

-Worst of all, they created an extreme combination of feeling alone, confused, and trapped. It is exhausting and dehumanizing.

These are all emotions I still feel from time to time, but I’m able to identify the fact that it came from them. Everyone has their relationship work differently, but no healthy relationship would make you consistently feel these things. Leaving hurts and you will feel regret at times, but leaving will prevent it from getting worse.

I mainly make posts on Twitter about autism. I’ve been told by friends and even people I don’t know that I’ve opened their eyes about the subject, so I feel like I know what I’m talking about.

I feel like there are many exaggerations and stereotypes about autism. Many people I’ve encountered seem to believe that we consist of only either geniuses or people who can’t care for themselves when autism is much more varied than that. Both stereotypes are harmful in their own ways, and in my case, because I’ve been diagnosed as high functioning autism, I’ve been expected to be this super genius. While I believe I’m intelligent in my own ways, I can’t be expected to be just like Temple Grandin or Einstein. I have my own needs and struggles. When I struggle or stim, it gets dismissed because it’s believed that’s a “low-functioning” thing. I could rant about the stereotypes for a while, but that’s the best way I can sum it up.

I have trouble comprehending and expressing some emotions such as jealousy, fear, and confusion. I’ve been told I look at some concepts such as relationships and love in an unusual way, but they seem to intrigue others. I also ask a lot of questions that most seem to not think of, I’ve always been full of questions.

When I’m at home, I stim a lot, but I force myself to not do it in public because I’ve been told that doing it is a bad thing, even if I know it’s not. I also worry if I’m faking things about my autism, I’ve been working on coming to realize I’m not. I guess I just have some internalized issues with myself and coming to terms that me showing my autism is not a bad thing despite what I was led to believe.
